A-List Actor Shares His Faith.
A true British Hollywood icon, James Fox has acted in major feature films alongside Mick Jagger, Anthony Hopkins, Johnny Depp, and many many more. I’m so lucky to have had 30 minutes of his time (he’s 85 now) to hear about his faith. This episode will be released this coming Monday. You may not know that when he was the most in-demand British actor back in the ‘70s - he quit it all to become an evangelical Christian. He took a few years out and then returned to acting, never again accepting a role where his newfound standards would be compromised. Although a slightly different episode than usual, I hope you’ll find value in James’s unique experiences and stalwart faith. This was a true honour for me.

A-List Actor Shares His Faith.
A true British Hollywood icon, James Fox has acted in major feature films alongside Mick Jagger, Anthony Hopkins, Johnny Depp, and many many more. I’m so lucky to have had 30 minutes of his time (he’s 85 now) to hear about his faith. This episode will be released this coming Monday. You may not know that when he was the most in-demand British actor back in the ‘70s - he quit it all to become an evangelical Christian. He took a few years out and then returned to acting, never again accepting a role where his newfound standards would be compromised. Although a slightly different episode than usual, I hope you’ll find value in James’s unique experiences and stalwart faith. This was a true honour for me.

**James William Fox** (born **William Fox**; 19 May 1939) is an English actor, known for his work in film and television. He is a member of the Fox family of actors. Fox's career began in the 1960s through leading roles in films such as _The Servant_ (1963), _King Rat_ (1965), _Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines_ (1965), _Thoroughly Modern Millie_ (1967), and _Performance_ (1970).
In the 1970s, Fox took a break from acting to focus on personal and spiritual matters, returning to acting in the early 1980s. Over time, he built a reputation for playing a variety of roles, including upper-class figures and more serious characters, notably in known for his roles in _A Passage to India_ (1984), _Patriot Games_ (1992), _The Remains of the Day_ (1993), _Jinnah_ (1998), _Sherlock Holmes_ (2009), and _Effie Gray_ (2014).
Fox won the BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles for his performance in _The Servant_, and was nominated for Best Actor in a Supporting Role for _A Passage to India_. He is also a Golden Globe Award nominee.

William Fox was born on 19 May 1939 in London, the second son of theatrical agentRobin Fox[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-1) and actress Angela Worthington. His elder brother is actor Edward Fox and his younger brother was film producer Robert Fox. Fox's maternal grandfather was playwright Frederick Lonsdale.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-foxes-2) He applied successfully to study acting at the Central School of Speech and Drama.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-cssd-3)
Fox first appeared on film as 11-year-old Toby Miniver in _The Miniver Story_ in 1950.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4) His early screen appearances, both in film and television, were made under his birth name, William Fox.
Fox appeared in the film _The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner_ (1962).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) His father, Robin, quarrelled bitterly with Tony Richardson over this, having attempted to forbid his friend from giving his son James (known as "Willie") a part in the film. His father claimed Willie had no talent for acting and should not give up his job in a bank.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-6)

In 1964, Fox won a BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles for _The Servant_ (1963), working alongside Dirk Bogarde, Sarah Miles, and Wendy Craig.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-bafta-1964-7) On 16 June 1965, Ken Annakin's period aviation film _Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines_ was released. In this British periodcomedy film, Fox is featured among an international ensemble cast including Stuart Whitman, Sarah Miles, Robert Morley, Terry-Thomas, Red Skelton, Benny Hill, Jean-Pierre Cassel, Gert Fröbe and Alberto Sordi.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-nytimes_066838-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-variety_1200420712-9) Some of the other films he acted in during this time are _King Rat_ (1965),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_The Chase_ (1966),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_Thoroughly Modern Millie_ (1967),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_Isadora_ (1968),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) and _Performance_ (1970).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4)

### Spiritual life and break from acting
[edit]
After finishing work on _Performance_ (released 1970, but shot in 1968),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) Fox suspended his acting career. The film, which starred Fox and Mick Jagger, was deemed so outrageous that critics at a preview screening walked out, with one film executive's wife reportedly throwing up in the cinema.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4)
In a 2008 interview, Fox said: "It was just part of my journey...I think my journey was to spend a while away from acting. And I never lost contact with it – watching movies, reading about it ... so I didn't feel I missed it."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tweed-10)
Fox became an evangelical Christian, working with the Navigators and devoting himself to the ministry.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-cinema-11) During this time, the only film in which Fox appeared was _No Longer Alone_ (1976), the story of Joan Winmill Brown,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-epit-12) a suicidal woman who was led to faith in Jesus Christ by Ruth Bell Graham.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-epit-12)

### Spiritual life and break from acting
After an absence from acting of several years, in 1981 Fox appeared on television in the _Play for Today_ "Country" by Trevor Griffiths, a comedy drama set against the 1945 UK parliamentary elections. On film he starred in Stephen Poliakoff's _Runners_ (1983),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_A Passage to India_ (1984),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) and _Comrades_ (1986).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He played Anthony Blunt in the BBC play by Alan Bennett, _A Question of Attribution_ (1992).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He also portrayed the character of Lord Holmes in _Patriot Games_ (1992), as well as Colonel Ferguson in _Farewell to the King_ (1989) and the Nazi-sympathising aristocrat Lord Darlington in _The Remains of the Day_ (1993).

### Spiritual life and break from acting
Fox has since appeared in the 2000 film _Sexy Beast_,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) the 2001 adaptation of _The Lost World_ as Prof. Leo Summerlee,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[Agatha Christie's Poirot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agatha\_Christie's\_Poirot "Agatha Christie's Poirot") – Death on the Nile_ (2004) as Colonel Race,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) and _Charlie and the Chocolate Factory_ (2005) as Mr. Salt, Veruca Salt's father.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He appeared in the _Doctor Who_audio drama_Shada_,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) and in 2007, Fox guest-starred in the British television crime series _Waking the Dead_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He also appeared opposite his son Laurence Fox in "Allegory of Love", an episode in the third series of _Lewis_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He was part of the cast of _Sherlock Holmes_ (2009), as Sir Thomas, leading member of a freemason-like secret society.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)

### Spiritual life and break from acting
In 2010, Fox filmed _Cleanskin_, a terrorist thriller directed by Hadi Hajaig.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-13) The following year, he played King George V in the film _[W.E.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W.E. **James William Fox** (born **William Fox**; 19 May 1939) is an English actor, known for his work in film and television. He is a member of the Fox family of actors. Fox's career began in the 1960s through leading roles in films such as _The Servant_ (1963), _King Rat_ (1965), _Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines_ (1965), _Thoroughly Modern Millie_ (1967), and _Performance_ (1970).
In the 1970s, Fox took a break from acting to focus on personal and spiritual matters, returning to acting in the early 1980s. Over time, he built a reputation for playing a variety of roles, including upper-class figures and more serious characters, notably in known for his roles in _A Passage to India_ (1984), _Patriot Games_ (1992), _The Remains of the Day_ (1993), _Jinnah_ (1998), _Sherlock Holmes_ (2009), and _Effie Gray_ (2014).
Fox won the BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles for his performance in _The Servant_, and was nominated for Best Actor in a Supporting Role for _A Passage to India_. He is also a Golden Globe Award nominee.
texts.1:
William Fox was born on 19 May 1939 in London, the second son of theatrical agentRobin Fox[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-1) and actress Angela Worthington. His elder brother is actor Edward Fox and his younger brother was film producer Robert Fox. Fox's maternal grandfather was playwright Frederick Lonsdale.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-foxes-2) He applied successfully to study acting at the Central School of Speech and Drama.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-cssd-3)
Fox first appeared on film as 11-year-old Toby Miniver in _The Miniver Story_ in 1950.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4) His early screen appearances, both in film and television, were made under his birth name, William Fox.
Fox appeared in the film _The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner_ (1962).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) His father, Robin, quarrelled bitterly with Tony Richardson over this, having attempted to forbid his friend from giving his son James (known as "Willie") a part in the film. His father claimed Willie had no talent for acting and should not give up his job in a bank.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-6)
texts.2: In 1964, Fox won a BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles for _The Servant_ (1963), working alongside Dirk Bogarde, Sarah Miles, and Wendy Craig.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-bafta-1964-7) On 16 June 1965, Ken Annakin's period aviation film _Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines_ was released. In this British periodcomedy film, Fox is featured among an international ensemble cast including Stuart Whitman, Sarah Miles, Robert Morley, Terry-Thomas, Red Skelton, Benny Hill, Jean-Pierre Cassel, Gert Fröbe and Alberto Sordi.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-nytimes_066838-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-variety_1200420712-9) Some of the other films he acted in during this time are _King Rat_ (1965),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_The Chase_ (1966),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_Thoroughly Modern Millie_ (1967),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_Isadora_ (1968),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) and _Performance_ (1970).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4)
texts.3:
### Spiritual life and break from acting
[edit]
After finishing work on _Performance_ (released 1970, but shot in 1968),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) Fox suspended his acting career. The film, which starred Fox and Mick Jagger, was deemed so outrageous that critics at a preview screening walked out, with one film executive's wife reportedly throwing up in the cinema.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4)
In a 2008 interview, Fox said: "It was just part of my journey...I think my journey was to spend a while away from acting. And I never lost contact with it – watching movies, reading about it ... so I didn't feel I missed it."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tweed-10)
Fox became an evangelical Christian, working with the Navigators and devoting himself to the ministry.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-cinema-11) During this time, the only film in which Fox appeared was _No Longer Alone_ (1976), the story of Joan Winmill Brown,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-epit-12) a suicidal woman who was led to faith in Jesus Christ by Ruth Bell Graham.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-epit-12)
texts.4:
### Spiritual life and break from acting
After an absence from acting of several years, in 1981 Fox appeared on television in the _Play for Today_ "Country" by Trevor Griffiths, a comedy drama set against the 1945 UK parliamentary elections. On film he starred in Stephen Poliakoff's _Runners_ (1983),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_A Passage to India_ (1984),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) and _Comrades_ (1986).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He played Anthony Blunt in the BBC play by Alan Bennett, _A Question of Attribution_ (1992).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He also portrayed the character of Lord Holmes in _Patriot Games_ (1992), as well as Colonel Ferguson in _Farewell to the King_ (1989) and the Nazi-sympathising aristocrat Lord Darlington in _The Remains of the Day_ (1993).
texts.5:
### Spiritual life and break from acting
Fox has since appeared in the 2000 film _Sexy Beast_,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) the 2001 adaptation of _The Lost World_ as Prof. Leo Summerlee,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[Agatha Christie's Poirot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agatha\_Christie's\_Poirot "Agatha Christie's Poirot") – Death on the Nile_ (2004) as Colonel Race,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) and _Charlie and the Chocolate Factory_ (2005) as Mr. Salt, Veruca Salt's father.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He appeared in the _Doctor Who_audio drama_Shada_,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) and in 2007, Fox guest-starred in the British television crime series _Waking the Dead_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He also appeared opposite his son Laurence Fox in "Allegory of Love", an episode in the third series of _Lewis_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He was part of the cast of _Sherlock Holmes_ (2009), as Sir Thomas, leading member of a freemason-like secret society.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)
